the_signal.headline: Workflow versioning now table stakes for production automation
the_signal.body: n8n's deep dive on Git-based versioning shows that automation reliability lives or dies on rollback capability and environment management—not just orchestration logic. GTM engineers shipping agent workflows into production need versioning built in from day one, not bolted on after outages. This is your safety net for rapid iteration without blowing up customer data pipelines.

tool_drop.name: n8n Workflow Versioning (Git-based)
tool_drop.what: Version control for automation workflows with rollback, environment management, and change tracking across production deployments.
tool_drop.why: GTM automation that fails silently costs revenue; versioning gives you the observability and rollback speed to iterate fast without customer impact.

thread_of_day.title: ETL vs ELT: Which pattern scales your GTM data stack?
thread_of_day.takeaway: ELT (extract, load, transform) beats ETL for modern GTM stacks because it keeps raw data queryable and lets you defer transformation logic until you know what you need.

quote.text: Track changes, manage environments, and roll back safely in production.
quote.source: n8n Blog — Workflow Versioning for Reliable Automation and Maintenance

whats_moving.context: Production automation is maturing past ad-hoc node wiring—teams now demand audit trails and safe rollbacks.
GTM teams handling enterprise deals now need automated evidence collection; manual compliance work is killing deal velocity.
n8n is aggressively positioning against legacy RPA tools by emphasizing reliability, scalability, and observability—GTM teams should know the difference when selling or building.

act_on_this: Audit your active agent/automation workflows for versioning capability—if you can't roll back a broken agent in under 2 minutes, add Git-based versioning this sprint.
